title: 1 m test lead with crocodile clips

sources.citation: International Annealed Copper Standard (IEC 60028, 1925): annealed copper has a resistivity of 1/58 Ω·mm²/m (1.7241 × 10⁻⁸ Ω·m) at 20 °C (293.15 K), and a temperature coefficient of resistance of 0.00393 per kelvin at 20 °C. The lead's resistance is computed from these (resistivity × length ÷ area, with the temperature coefficient), never taken from a conductor table.

0.75 mm² is one of the standard nominal conductor cross-sections (the IEC 60228 series of nominal areas) and is common for flexible test leads. The area is nominal and stranding is ignored; IEC 60228's resistance values are not used.
game-design: a 1 m bench test lead, a common retail length.

game-design, pending electrical-realism review: about 5 mΩ where a sprung crocodile clip grips a clean terminal, chosen as an order of magnitude. F2.1, which first uses it, confirms it against a published source or replaces it.
